contracts.historicalIntent: Object lifecycle: Objects own deterministic destruction, rectangle math follows half-open bounds, and ordered collections preserve their documented comparison behavior.
contracts.observedBehavior: Object lifecycle: Managed object, geometry, and generic collection types preserve the tested behavioral results without raw ownership.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Managed lifetime, generic collections, and exceptions replace raw pointers while preserving observable results.
contracts.risk: Changes to equality, ordering, or disposal can affect all higher framework layers.

contracts.historicalIntent: Typed event channels: Events carry one active channel, numeric commands keep stable identity, and dispatch stops after explicit consumption.
contracts.observedBehavior: Typed factories usually keep one active channel, but CreateMouse accepts composite mouse masks and therefore permits an event value that is not one concrete dispatch kind.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Managed factories remain the intended modernization; their input validation must still preserve the one-concrete-kind invariant.
contracts.risk: A composite kind can enter more than one dispatch channel and makes event consumption ambiguous.

contracts.historicalIntent: Command identity: Events carry one active channel, numeric commands keep stable identity, and dispatch stops after explicit consumption.
contracts.observedBehavior: Command identity: Typed event factories, named command constants, and ordered group handling preserve event and command semantics.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Factories, records, and managed payloads replace unions and raw information pointers.
contracts.risk: A shared numeric command namespace and incorrect event clearing can misroute input.

contracts.historicalIntent: Ordered dispatch: Events carry one active channel, numeric commands keep stable identity, and dispatch stops after explicit consumption.
contracts.observedBehavior: Ordered dispatch: Typed event factories, named command constants, and ordered group handling preserve event and command semantics.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None
contracts.risk: A shared numeric command namespace and incorrect event clearing can misroute input.

contracts.historicalIntent: Ownership and lifecycle: Groups own children, maintain one current view, propagate state, and release children in defined order.
contracts.observedBehavior: Ownership and lifecycle: TGroup and TView enforce owner membership, focus transfer, state propagation, and managed shutdown invariants.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Managed references and explicit guards replace circular raw-pointer ownership without changing focus order.
contracts.risk: Incorrect owner or focus state can orphan views or deliver events to the wrong target.

contracts.historicalIntent: Focus transition: Groups own children, maintain one current view, propagate state, and release children in defined order.
contracts.observedBehavior: TGroup transfers Current and Focused state, but the current focus path does not integrate child validation as a veto before focus leaves an invalid input control.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None
contracts.risk: Focus can leave invalid input and move command delivery to a target that should not yet become current.

contracts.historicalIntent: Hierarchy and state propagation: Groups own children, maintain one current view, propagate state, and release children in defined order.
contracts.observedBehavior: TGroup propagates Focused and Disabled to all direct children, while the historical contract limits Focused to Current and applies state-specific propagation rules.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None
contracts.risk: Several children can appear focused or disabled through group state even though only one current child owns focus.

contracts.historicalIntent: Coordinate transformation: Views translate local and global coordinates, clip output, grow with owners, and redraw only exposed regions.
contracts.observedBehavior: Coordinate transformation: View coordinates and scroll models clamp movement, update bounds, and protect redraw visibility through managed buffers.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None
contracts.risk: Off-by-one bounds or clipping errors can hide or overwrite visible cells.

contracts.historicalIntent: Growth and scrolling: Views translate local and global coordinates, clip output, grow with owners, and redraw only exposed regions.
contracts.observedBehavior: Growth and scrolling: View coordinates and scroll models clamp movement, update bounds, and protect redraw visibility through managed buffers.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Bounds and scroll state use safe managed arithmetic and explicit clamping.
contracts.risk: Off-by-one bounds or clipping errors can hide or overwrite visible cells.

contracts.historicalIntent: Clipping and exposure: Views translate local and global coordinates, clip output, grow with owners, and redraw only exposed regions.

contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None

contracts.historicalIntent: Application loop: The program loop obtains and dispatches events, the desktop owns windows, and modal execution returns one command result.
contracts.observedBehavior: TProgram provides a deterministic queue and dispatch loop, but it has no pending-event or Idle lifecycle hook required by both reviewed demo families for background refresh and command-state updates.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None
contracts.risk: Applications must emulate idle work outside the framework, which can starve refresh work or duplicate event-loop policy.

contracts.historicalIntent: Desktop and window stack: The program loop obtains and dispatches events, the desktop owns windows, and modal execution returns one command result.
contracts.observedBehavior: TDesktop owns child views, but current APIs and proofs do not establish insertion, top-window selection, tiling, cascading, and close-all behavior used by the reviewed Wave-5 and Wave-6 applications.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None
contracts.risk: Later examples could add local window-stack substitutes or expose inconsistent focus and geometry behavior.

contracts.historicalIntent: Modality and window close: The program loop obtains and dispatches events, the desktop owns windows, and modal execution returns one command result.
contracts.observedBehavior: TWindow emits cmClose to its owner for Ctrl+W or Escape, but the default desktop path does not remove the window, and there is no complete ExecView or ExecuteDialog modal lifecycle with focus restoration.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Explicit close decisions and a managed event loop remain valid modernization goals, but the observable lifecycle must complete rather than stop at a signal.
contracts.risk: Keyboard close can appear successful while the window remains active, and modal callers lack a stable result and focus boundary.

contracts.historicalIntent: Menu navigation: Menus navigate enabled entries, status definitions expose executable commands, and keyboard shortcuts remain visible.
contracts.observedBehavior: Menu navigation: TMenuBar and TStatusLine expose keyboard navigation, command execution, disabled-state truth, and structured shortcuts.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None
contracts.risk: Disabled commands or shortcut drift can expose unavailable actions or break keyboard access.

contracts.historicalIntent: Status and command enablement: Menus navigate enabled entries, status definitions expose executable commands, and keyboard shortcuts remain visible.
contracts.observedBehavior: Menu and status items expose local Enabled state, but the framework has no shared command-state set and no event-loop refresh contract for enabling actions from the active window and selection state.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Structured shortcut queries and explicit enabled state make command truth immutable and accessible.
contracts.risk: Menus, status lines, and focused views can disagree about whether one command is currently executable.

contracts.historicalIntent: Shortcuts and help description: Menus navigate enabled entries, status definitions expose executable commands, and keyboard shortcuts remain visible.
contracts.observedBehavior: Shortcuts and help description: TMenuBar and TStatusLine expose keyboard navigation, command execution, disabled-state truth, and structured shortcuts.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Structured shortcut queries and explicit enabled state make command truth immutable and accessible.
contracts.risk: Disabled commands or shortcut drift can expose unavailable actions or break keyboard access.

contracts.historicalIntent: Dialog state and validation: Dialogs preserve control state, validate before acceptance, and controls consume activation and editing input predictably.
contracts.observedBehavior: TDialog closes for every command event, and its standard Valid path does not walk child controls before accepting a completion command.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None
contracts.risk: Unrelated commands can terminate a dialog and invalid child state can be accepted without a visible rejection boundary.

contracts.historicalIntent: Control activation: Dialogs preserve control state, validate before acceptance, and controls consume activation and editing input predictably.
contracts.observedBehavior: Control activation: Dialogs and controls preserve state through validation, rejection, activation, input, selection, and explicit fallback.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: None
contracts.risk: Partial validation or state mutation can accept invalid data or discard user input.

contracts.historicalIntent: Selection, input, and color: Dialogs preserve control state, validate before acceptance, and controls consume activation and editing input predictably.
contracts.observedBehavior: TInputLine edits managed text, but it has no validator attachment or focus-loss rejection path even though validator types and dialog-level validation exist separately.
contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Managed state and explicit validator objects remain the intended design; they need a real input-control integration boundary.
contracts.risk: Validation helpers can exist while user input bypasses them during focus transfer and dialog acceptance.

contracts.historicalIntent: Editor and clipboard: Editors mutate buffers, clipboard commands preserve text, file dialogs separate selection from I/O, and close paths protect modified data.

contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Managed strings, isolated clipboard state, explicit file decisions, and conflict snapshots prevent implicit data loss.

contracts.modernCSharpRationale: Managed strings, isolated clipboard state, explicit file decisions, and conflict snapshots prevent implicit data loss.

findings.observation: CreateMouse accepts composite mouse masks instead of requiring one concrete mouse event kind.
findings.reproduction: Call TEvent.CreateMouse with a bitwise combination of MouseDown and MouseMove and observe that the factory accepts the ambiguous kind.
findings.impact: Dispatch and consumption can no longer rely on one active event channel.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Reject masks and mixed channels at construction while preserving every supported concrete event factory.
findings.nonGoals: No command-number redesign and no native event-union recreation.

findings.observation: Focus transfer is not coupled to child validation, so an invalid input can lose focus without a rejection boundary.
findings.reproduction: Attach an invalid input scenario to a dialog, request focus on another selectable child, and observe that TGroup completes the transition without validator-owned veto.
findings.impact: Dialog and file workflows can move command focus away from invalid state and later accept it.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Prove one current child, ordered focus broadcasts, and a validator-owned veto that preserves focus and input state.
findings.nonGoals: No visual redesign and no pointer-only focus interaction.

findings.observation: TGroup propagates Focused and Disabled uniformly to every child instead of applying state-specific hierarchy rules.
findings.reproduction: Set Focused on a group with multiple children and observe that all direct children receive Focused rather than only Current.
findings.impact: View state, rendering, focus announcements, and command routing can report several focused children.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Implement and test state-specific propagation for Focused, Disabled, Active, Dragging, Exposed, and Current without changing ownership semantics.
findings.nonGoals: No mechanical C++ layout port and no new view-tree abstraction.

findings.observation: The application loop has no bounded pending-event and Idle lifecycle contract.
findings.reproduction: Compare TProgram.GetEvent and Run with the clock, heap, command-state, and incremental directory refresh work in the reviewed consumers; no framework hook can schedule that work when the queue is empty.
findings.impact: Wave applications would need local polling loops or would omit required background refresh behavior.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Provide deterministic idle invocation only when no event is pending, with non-busy proof and testable scheduling boundaries.
findings.nonGoals: No background thread requirement and no platform-specific message pump.

findings.observation: Desktop ownership exists, but insertion, top-window, tile, cascade, and close-all contracts are not available or proven as one coherent stack model.
findings.reproduction: Map TVDEMO and TVFM window commands to current TDesktop APIs; the required operations cannot be expressed and proven without consumer-local orchestration.
findings.impact: Wave ports risk duplicating stack, focus, geometry, and close policy in application code.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Define a bounded desktop stack API and prove focus-preserving insert, select-next, tile, cascade, and safe close-all behavior.
findings.nonGoals: No reproduction of DOS memory management and no application-specific window classes.

findings.observation: Default keyboard close stops at a cmClose signal and the framework lacks a complete modal execution lifecycle with result and focus restoration.
findings.reproduction: Run a TWindow under the default desktop, send Ctrl+W or Escape, and observe that the owner receives cmClose while the window remains; no ExecView or ExecuteDialog equivalent completes a modal child lifecycle.
findings.impact: Visible windows can fail to close and dialogs cannot offer a reusable deterministic result boundary.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Prove default close removal, safe-close veto, modal result propagation, event isolation, and previous-focus restoration through the real application loop.
findings.nonGoals: No nested native message loop and no silent discard of modified data.

findings.observation: Commands have per-item Enabled flags but no shared command-state contract refreshed from active context.
findings.reproduction: Model TVDEMO or TVFM selection-dependent commands with current menus and status lines; each surface must be updated separately and no idle or focus notification proves consistency.
findings.impact: Keyboard, menu, status-line, and focused-view command availability can disagree.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Provide one testable command-state source and prove synchronized menu, status, keyboard, and active-view behavior after focus and selection changes.
findings.nonGoals: No application command catalog and no removal of explicit Enabled state.

findings.observation: The real TProgram console path bypasses TKeyCodeTranslator for most keys and disagrees with TWindow about modifier bit values.
findings.reproduction: Feed ConsoleKeyInfo through TProgram.GetEvent for a non-F10 function key or Ctrl+W and compare the result with TKeyCodeTranslator and TShiftState; injected normalized event tests do not cover this path.
findings.impact: Keyboard commands can pass unit tests and still fail in an interactive terminal.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Route real ingress through one translator and prove printable, navigation, function, Alt, Ctrl, Shift, and fallback keys end to end.
findings.nonGoals: No platform-specific scan-code table outside the compatibility boundary.

findings.observation: The framework proves title-bar drag only and has no generic tracked drag session for list and file drag-and-drop.
findings.reproduction: Map TVFM DragDrop and FileView flows to current mouse APIs; there is no shared capture, movement threshold, cancellation, target negotiation, or keyboard fallback contract.
findings.impact: Wave 6 would need pointer-only local behavior that is difficult to test and inaccessible from the keyboard.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Deliver a bounded generic drag session with capture, threshold, cancel, drop result, keyboard-equivalent command, and app-loop proof.
findings.nonGoals: No mandatory mouse-only workflow and no full desktop drag-and-drop protocol.

findings.observation: TDialog handles every command as a completion request and standard Valid does not validate child controls.
findings.reproduction: Send an unrelated command to a dialog and observe completion, then use a standard dialog with invalid child state and observe that no child-validation walk blocks acceptance.
findings.impact: Dialogs can close unexpectedly and accept invalid data.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Only explicit completion commands may close, and acceptance must prove child validation, rejection state preservation, and focus on the failing control.
findings.nonGoals: No application-specific dialog command list and no visual redesign.

findings.observation: TInputLine and TValidator are separate APIs without an attachment, transfer, focus-loss, or acceptance integration contract.
findings.reproduction: Create a validator and an input line, then attempt to bind them using public APIs; no path exists for validator-owned edit, transfer, or focus-loss rejection.
findings.impact: Consumer validators can be defined but cannot reliably guard actual user input.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Expose a modern validator attachment and prove edit, transfer, focus-loss, dialog acceptance, error indication, and state-preserving rejection.
findings.nonGoals: No raw-pointer transfer model and no requirement to copy every historical validator subclass.

findings.observation: File-dialog completion does not prove mode-aware validation for wildcard, directory, missing open target, and save target cases.
findings.reproduction: Confirm a typed missing path through the current standard dialog flow and observe a valid decision without an operation-specific rejection boundary.
findings.impact: Callers can receive invalid selections and must duplicate path policy.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Prove explicit mode-aware results for navigation, wildcard expansion, existing open targets, new save targets, conflicts, cancellation, and invalid manual paths.
findings.nonGoals: No arbitrary user-file reads in tests and no destructive file operation.

findings.observation: Named resources are proven for help and dialog descriptions, but not for reconstructible menu, status-line, and dialog composition.
findings.reproduction: Attempt to express the TVRDEMO, GENRDEMO, and TVFM named UI-resource flows with registered resource types and round-trip tests; required composition contracts are absent or unproven.
findings.impact: Consumers may hard-code reusable UI resources or persist unsupported object graphs.
findings.acceptanceBoundary: Choose and prove an explicit modern description or registration model for named menu, status-line, and dialog resources with strict malformed-input rejection.
findings.nonGoals: No binary compatibility with historical resource files and no arbitrary runtime type activation.
